findings.claim: Item 24 says '[p] : Pic^0_{X′} → Pic^0_{X′} is a finite étale H^1_ét(X′, μ_p)-torsor'. This copies Corollary 2.19's 'More precisely' clause, which is false whenever NS(X′) has p-torsion. The kernel of [p] on Pic^0_{X′} is Pic^0_{X′}[p] = Pic^0_{X′} ∩ H^1_ét(X′, μ_p), which can be a proper subgroup. Counterexample: X = Y^an for an Enriques surface Y over K, B = O_X (so X′ = X) and p = 2. Then Pic^0_{X′} = 0, since H^1(Y, O) = 0 and char K = 0, but H^1_ét(X, μ_2) = Pic(Y)[2] = Z/2. The proof's surjectivity step is also incomplete: the Kummer sequence shows Pic^0 ⊆ [p](Pic_{X′}), not Pic^0 ⊆ [p](Pic^0). The 'finite étale' conclusion, which is all that is used later, remains true.
findings.evidence: v3 p. 13, Corollary 2.19: 'If PicX′ = R1π′∗O× is representable, then [p] : Pic0X′ → Pic0X′ is finite étale. More precisely, it is an étale torsor under H1ét(X′, µp).' Proof: 'By Proposition 2.18, the last map goes from a rigid group to a constant group, so it sends Pic0X′ to 0. Hence [p] is surjective on Pic0X′.' For the Enriques surface: the Kummer sequence gives 0 → K^×/K^×2 = 0 → H^1(Y, μ_2) → Pic(Y)[2] = Z/2 → 0. Pic_Y is étale, so Pic^0_Y is trivial. Finite étale cohomology is unchanged by analytification, and Pic_{X} = (Pic_Y)^an by §2.2.

findings.claim: The brief presents Heuer's Proposition 2.18 (R^m g_*(Z/n) = H^m(Z, Z/n) on smooth rigid spaces) as Bhatt–Hansen's Theorem 3.15 and tells the design job to import 'Huber's proper-support theory from ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H3'. Bhatt–Hansen's Theorem 3.15 is base change for a proper map in a Cartesian square, for Zariski-constructible complexes. Huber's theorem, which H3 plans, covers only p ∤ n. The n = p^a case that Heuer needs uses Bhatt–Hansen's Theorem 3.10 (proper pushforward preserves Zariski-constructibility, hence overconvergence), Huber's stalk formula, and Lemma 3.25, which rests on the primitive comparison theorem for proper rigid spaces. The brief names none of these inputs. It also does not say that Z here is proper but possibly singular and non-reduced (Heuer's spectral variety X′), which is outside a Part II titled for smooth proper spaces.

findings.claim: Item 15 copies the paper's §3.3 claim that the topological p-torsion subgroup Ĝ is "an analytic p-divisible group when [p] is surjective ([24, Prop. 6.10])". This is false in general: the cited Proposition 6.10 gives only that the identity component Ĝ° is analytic p-divisible ((2) ⇒ (4)). The paper's sentence rests on v1 of Heuer–Werner–Zhang, which claimed (1) ⇔ (2) ([p] surjective implies [p] finite étale surjective); v2 (17 March 2025) restricts (2) ⇒ (1) to π_0(G) finite. Counterexample: G = ⊕_{n∈ℕ} Q_p/Z_p as a constant rigid group (a disjoint union of points). [p] is surjective and Ĝ = G, but G[p] = ⊕_ℕ Z/p is infinite, so [p] is not finite and Ĝ is not analytic p-divisible (HWZ Definition 6.8(1) requires G = Ĝ and [p] finite surjective). Nothing downstream breaks: the logarithm sequence holds anyway (HWZ Prop. 6.5(2) and 6.10, (2) ⇒ (7)), and Theorem 3.20 is applied only to connected groups. The paper's mistake is not in sourceIssues.

findings.claim: Item 16 states Theorem 3.20 with the paper's hypothesis "[p] surjective on K-points" and attributes it to HWZ Thm. 6.12. HWZ Thm. 6.12 (v1 and v2) assumes G locally p-divisible, and surjectivity on K-points does not imply that. Counterexample: V := ⋃_{c∈K} {x : |x − c| ≤ 1} ⊂ G_a is an open rigid subgroup with V(K) = K, so [p] is surjective on K-points. Its logarithm is the inclusion V ↪ G_a (unique by HWZ Prop. 6.5(2)), which is not surjective: a point t over a larger field with distance > 1 from K is not in V. So V is not locally p-divisible (HWZ Prop. 6.10, (5) ⇔ (7)), and the cited theorem does not cover the statement as printed. findings.claim: Section 1.1 defines 'an exponential for K' as a continuous splitting of log : 1 + m_K → K. Definition 3.19, and Heuer–Werner–Zhang Def. 6.1, which Theorem 3.20 relies on, also require Exp|_{p^α m_K} = exp, and continuity does not imply this. Counterexample: let χ : K → μ_{p^∞} be a nonzero F_p-linear form on p^α m_K / p^{α+1} m_K ≅ m_K/pm_K, composed with F_p ≅ μ_p and extended to K, which is possible because μ_{p^∞} is divisible. Then χ is continuous, since its kernel contains the open subgroup p^{α+1}m_K, and Exp·χ is a continuous splitting of log that is not exp on p^α m_K. Item 4 correctly follows Definition 3.19, but the reader report repeats the weaker phrase. Also: The report glosses an exponential for K as "a continuous splitting of log : 1 + m_K → K". That is weaker than Definition 3.19, which also requires Exp to restrict to the convergent exp on p^α m_K. If Exp_0 is an exponential and χ : K → μ_{p^∞} is a character trivial on p^β m_K (β > α) but not on p^α m_K, then Exp_0 · χ is a continuous splitting of log that is not an exponential. Such χ exist because p^α m_K/p^β m_K is a nonzero p-primary group and μ_{p^∞} is divisible. Item 4 has the right definition.
